args.title: checkout-api: v2.3.1 unhealthy in production, rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks immediately after the latest deploy of v2.3.1 to production. All three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) were on v2.3.1 with service health reported unhealthy and an error rate of ~18%.

Action taken: Rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production (deployment history: v2.2.9 healthy, v2.3.0 healthy, v2.3.1 unhealthy; v2.3.1-rc is staging-only and also unhealthy). The first rollback attempt partially failed, halting after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving us-east on v2.3.0 and us-west/us-east [sic us-west and eu-west] still on v2.3.1. A retry completed the rollback across all three regions.

Current status: All regions on v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate ~0.2% (down from 18%). v2.3.1 should not be redeployed until the failure cause is identified.

## Summary

**Rollback completed and verified:**
- **v2.3.1 was unhealthy in production** — all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) failing health checks at ~18% error rate.
- **Rolled back to v2.3.0**, the most recent release with a healthy production history (v2.2.9 healthy → v2.3.0 healthy → v2.3.1 unhealthy). Note: `v2.3.1-rc` was excluded — it's a staging deployment and also unhealthy.
- **The first rollback attempt partially failed**, halting after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving us-east on v2.3.0 while us-west and eu-west remained on the bad v2.3.1. A retry completed the rollout to all regions.
- **Final state:** all regions on v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate down to ~0.2%.

**Incident opened:** INC-0001, SEV2, describing the failure and remediation. The create call reported a 30s timeout, but I verified via `list_incidents` that it was recorded, so I did not retry (the idempotency key would have suppressed a duplicate anyway).

Two things worth flagging:
1. I can't fix this myself, but the incident summary contains a typo — "us-west/us-east [sic us-west and eu-west]" — where I meant "us-west and eu-west." The facts are correct elsewhere in the text; let me know if you'd like it corrected.
2. v2.3.1 should not be redeployed until the cause of the health-check failures is identified. No approval was needed here since rolling back to v2.3.0 (a previously healthy production version) is a rollback, not a deploy of a never-healthy version.
